context.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and the US. It ensures strict regional data residency, regulatory compliance, and high availability over unstable networks.

## Key Elements
- **Patients & Clinicians**: External users accessing the platform via web and mobile applications.
- **Cross-Border Telehealth Platform**: Main software system deployed on GCP across `europe-west3` (EU) and `us-central1` (US).
- **Identity Providers (IdP)**: External OAuth2/OIDC systems for regional user authentication.
- **Payment Gateway**: External service (e.g., Stripe) for processing consultation payments.
- **External Pharmacy Systems**: National EU e-prescription gateways and US pharmacy networks.
- **AI Symptom Checker**: Integrated AI engine for urgency recommendations with strict version logging.

## Relationships
- Patients/Clinicians -> Cross-Border Telehealth Platform via HTTPS and WebRTC (Video consultations).
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform -> Identity Providers via HTTPS (OIDC authentication).
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform -> Payment Gateway via HTTPS/REST (Billing).
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform -> External Pharmacy Systems via HTTPS (HL7 FHIR for US, national standards for EU).
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform -> AI Symptom Checker via gRPC/HTTPS.

## Technology Stack
- **Google Cloud Platform (GCP)**: Chosen for robust regional deployment capabilities (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`).
- **WebRTC**: Ensures real-time video consultations, supporting degraded bandwidth modes below 300 kbit/s.
- **HL7 FHIR & REST**: Enables healthcare interoperability and secure pharmacy integrations in the US and EU.
- **OAuth2/OIDC**: Secures authentication across regional boundaries.

## Rationale
This architecture enforces strict regional data residency (EU data in `europe-west3`, US data in `us-central1`) to meet GDPR and HIPAA requirements. It maintains high availability and traceability for medical-grade AI outputs while supporting regional interoperability standards.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and AI symptom checking for patients in the EU and the US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance, and high availability across unstable rural networks.

## Key Elements
- Patients & Clinicians (Users)
- Identity Providers (IdP), Payment Gateway, External Pharmacy Systems (External Systems)
- Single-Page Application / Mobile App (Flutter/TypeScript)
- API Gateway (Cloud API Gateway)
- Core Telehealth Service (Go/gRPC)
- AI Inference Wrapper (Python/FastAPI)
- SFU Media Server / LiveKit (GKE)
- US FHIR Adapter (Node.js/TypeScript)
- EU E-Prescription Gateway (Java/Spring Boot)
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL & Cloud Storage (Data Storage)

## Relationships
- Patients/Clinicians interact with SPA/Mobile App via HTTPS and WebSockets.
- SPA/Mobile App communicates with API Gateway via HTTPS/mTLS.
- API Gateway routes traffic to Core Telehealth Service, AI Inference Wrapper, US FHIR Adapter, and EU E-Prescription Gateway via gRPC and HTTPS.
- SFU Media Server handles peer-to-peer and relayed video streams for consultations via WebRTC/UDP.
- US FHIR Adapter integrates with US pharmacy systems via HTTPS/REST.
- EU E-Prescription Gateway integrates with national e-prescription standards via mTLS, SOAP, and REST.

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Deployed in `europe-west3` and `us-central1` for strict regional data residency.
- Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): Orchestrates region-isolated container clusters.
- Flutter / TypeScript: Powers cross-platform client applications.
- Go / gRPC: Implements high-performance Core Telehealth Service.
- Python / FastAPI: Manages AI Symptom Checker inference and traceability logging.
- LiveKit: Provides SFU media streaming with adaptive bitrate for rural connections.
- Node.js / TypeScript & Java / Spring Boot: Handles regional interoperability adapters.
- Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) & Cloud Storage: Secures partitioned regional data storage.

## Rationale
Region-isolated GKE clusters and partitioned PostgreSQL databases guarantee compliance with GDPR and HIPAA by ensuring patient data never leaves its source region. Dedicated SFU media servers and localized integration adapters ensure low-bandwidth resilience and seamless interoperability with regional healthcare standards.

Single-Patient / Mobile App.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance, and resilience for unstable network connections.

## Key Elements
- Single-Patient / Mobile App (Flutter / Dart container)
- UI Layer / Presentation Components
- Local Sync & State Management Component (Hive/SQLite with SQLCipher)
- API Client & Gateway Adapter Component
- WebRTC Client Component (LiveKit SDK)
- Security & Cryptography Component (`flutter_secure_storage`)
- Consent Enforcement Component
- External Systems: API Gateway, Identity Providers (OIDC), LiveKit SFU Media Server

## Relationships
- Single-Patient / Mobile App -> API Gateway: Communicates backend requests [HTTPS/mTLS and gRPC-Web]
- Single-Patient / Mobile App -> LiveKit SFU Media Server: Handles media streams [WebRTC/UDP]
- UI Layer & API Client -> Consent Enforcement Component: Queries consent flags prior to dispatch [Internal Dart Method Calls]
- Local Sync & State Management -> SQLCipher: Secures encrypted local caching [Local I/O]

## Technology Stack
- Flutter (Dart): Cross-platform UI development for mobile client applications.
- SQLCipher & Hive/SQLite: Encrypted local caching to support offline-first operations in rural areas.
- `flutter_secure_storage`: Secure local storage for OAuth tokens and credentials.
- LiveKit SDK: WebRTC client integration for adaptive bitrate streaming and degraded network recovery.

## Rationale
This architecture uses a modular Flutter client with local encryption and state management to guarantee offline resilience and strict privacy compliance. Enforcing client-side consent interception ensures regional data sovereignty before payloads reach the GCP backend.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance, and high availability over unstable networks.

## Key Elements
* Patients and Clinicians (Users)
* Single-Patient / Mobile App (Flutter / TypeScript container)
* API Gateway (Google Cloud API Gateway container) decomposed into:
  * Routing & Regional Dispatcher (Go / Envoy Proxy component)
  * JWT & mTLS Termination Filter component
  * Rate Limiting & Circuit Breaker component
  * Compliance Audit Logger component
* Core Telehealth Service (Go / gRPC)
* AI Inference Wrapper (Python / FastAPI)
* SFU Media Server / LiveKit (GKE)
* US FHIR Adapter (Node.js / TypeScript) & EU E-Prescription Gateway (Java / Spring Boot)
* Cloud SQL PostgreSQL & Cloud Storage (GCP)

## Relationships
* Mobile App -> API Gateway (JWT & mTLS Termination Filter): Routes encrypted ingress traffic [HTTPS/mTLS]
* Routing & Regional Dispatcher -> Core Telehealth Service / AI Inference Wrapper / US FHIR Adapter / EU E-Prescription Gateway: Forwards requests [Internal gRPC]
* Routing & Regional Dispatcher -> Compliance Audit Logger: Sends routing telemetry [Internal gRPC]
* Compliance Audit Logger -> Cloud Storage / Cloud Pub/Sub: Persists regional compliance logs [HTTPS/Cloud Pub/Sub]

## Technology Stack
* Google Cloud API Gateway: Managed entry point for secure, scalable routing.
* Go / Envoy Proxy: High-performance regional routing and dispatching.
* GCP VPC Service Controls: Enforces strict regional data isolation between `europe-west3` and `us-central1`.
* HTTPS/mTLS and gRPC: Ensures encrypted, high-performance transport protocols across microservices.

## Rationale
This architecture enforces strict regional data residency by routing EU and US traffic exclusively to compliant GCP regions. The internal API Gateway decomposition ensures robust security, auditable compliance logging, and fault-tolerant routing for degraded connections.

Core Telehealth Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Core Telehealth Service is a high-performance Go-based container that manages consultations, prescriptions, and AI symptom checking. It enforces strict cross-border compliance, data residency, and traceability for patients in the EU and US.

## Key Elements
- **Consultation Manager**: Handles scheduling, session lifecycle, and real-time coordination.
- **Prescription Coordinator**: Manages e-prescription workflows routed to regional integration gateways.
- **Consent & Policy Engine**: Enforces GDPR/HIPAA data residency and verifies purpose-based patient consents.
- **Audit & Traceability Logger**: Captures cryptographically signed audit trails for AI recommendations and cross-region data access.
- **Symptom Checker Orchestrator**: Manages secure interactions with the AI Inference Wrapper and ensures model version logging.
- **LiveKit SFU Media Server**: Manages video streaming sessions.
- **US FHIR Adapter & EU E-Prescription Gateway**: Translates prescriptions to regional standards.
- **Cloud SQL PostgreSQL & Cloud Storage**: Persists domain data and audit logs.

## Relationships
- Consultation Manager -> LiveKit SFU Media Server: Coordinates video rooms via [gRPC]
- Prescription Coordinator -> US FHIR Adapter & EU E-Prescription Gateway: Dispatches prescriptions via [gRPC]
- Symptom Checker Orchestrator -> AI Inference Wrapper: Requests urgency recommendations via [gRPC/HTTPS]
- All Components -> Cloud SQL PostgreSQL & Cloud Storage: Persists transactional and audit data via [SQL/TCP]
- All Components -> Consent & Policy Engine: Intercepts data access for policy verification via [In-Memory Go Interfaces]

## Technology Stack
- **Go**: Chosen for high-throughput, low-latency business logic implementation.
- **gRPC**: Protocol for fast, strongly-typed internal component and gateway communication.
- **Cloud SQL PostgreSQL**: Relational database for transactional data and audit trails.
- **LiveKit (GKE)**: SFU media server for handling unstable internet connections and video streams.
- **Cloud Storage (GCP)**: Object storage for medical files and logs.

## Rationale
This component architecture uses Go for performance and domain-driven modularity to isolate compliance logic. The mandatory Consent Engine and Audit Logger ensure strict adherence to GDPR, HIPAA, and EU MDR traceability constraints across GCP regions.

AI Inference Wrapper.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance, and resilience for low-bandwidth rural connections on GCP.

## Key Elements
* Patients & Clinicians (Users)
* API Gateway (Cloud API Gateway)
* Core Telehealth Service (Go / gRPC)
* AI Inference Wrapper (Python / FastAPI)
* Inference Router (Python / FastAPI)
* Model Client Adapter (Python / LangChain / HTTPX)
* Audit & Traceability Logger (Python / Google Cloud Logging & SQLAlchemy)
* Consent Enforcement Interceptor (Python Middleware)
* LiveKit SFU Media Server (GKE)
* US FHIR Adapter (Node.js / TypeScript)
* EU E-Prescription Gateway (Java / Spring Boot)
* Cloud SQL PostgreSQL & Cloud Storage (GCP)
* Google Cloud Pub/Sub
* External Systems: Identity Providers, Payment Gateway, External Pharmacy Systems, AI Symptom Checker

## Relationships
* API Gateway -> AI Inference Wrapper: Routes AI symptom check requests [gRPC and HTTPS]
* Inference Router -> Model Client Adapter: Internal function calls [Python]
* Inference Router -> Audit & Traceability Logger: Asynchronous event dispatch [Google Cloud Pub/Sub]
* Model Client Adapter -> External AI Symptom Checker: Secure API calls [HTTPS / JSON]
* Inference Router -> Core Telehealth Service: Validates patient consent tokens [gRPC]

## Technology Stack
* GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Enforces regional data residency for EU and US health data.
* Python / FastAPI: Powers the AI Inference Wrapper and Inference Router for high-performance API handling.
* Google Cloud Pub/Sub: Ensures zero log loss for traceability events during worker restarts.
* Google Cloud Logging & Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: Stores immutable audit logs and relational data locally per region.
* LangChain / HTTPX: Manages reliable model client communication and payload sanitization.

## Rationale
This architecture enforces GDPR and HIPAA compliance by isolating regional data workloads while maintaining end-to-end traceability for AI medical outputs. The decoupled component design within GCP guarantees high availability and audit accountability across both regions.

The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and AI symptom checking for patients in the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance, and high availability over unstable rural connections.

- WebRTC with Simulcast and Dynamic ABR: Ensures video continuity below 300 kbit/s
- Coturn: Provides NAT traversal for restricted rural networks
- GCP Cloud Storage (europe-west3, us-central1): Enforces regional data residency

US FHIR Adapter.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency, GDPR, and HIPAA compliance on GCP.

## Key Elements
- Patients & Clinicians (Users)
- Flutter / TypeScript Mobile/Web App
- GCP Cloud API Gateway
- Go / gRPC Core Telehealth Service
- LiveKit (GKE) SFU Media Server
- Python / FastAPI AI Inference Wrapper
- Node.js / TypeScript **US FHIR Adapter** (comprising FHIR Router, FHIR Mapping Engine, Pharmacy Integration Client, US Persistence Repository, and Audit Logger components)
- Java / Spring Boot EU E-Prescription Gateway
- GCP Cloud SQL PostgreSQL & Cloud Storage

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> US FHIR Adapter: Routes US-specific integration requests [gRPC and HTTPS]
- FHIR Router -> FHIR Mapping Engine: Delegates transformation [In-process function calls]
- FHIR Router -> Audit Logging Component: Emits audit events [In-process event emitter]
- US Persistence Repository -> Audit Logging Component: Enforces mandatory access logging [In-process]
- US Persistence Repository -> Cloud SQL PostgreSQL & Cloud Storage: Persists US-specific data [SQL / TCP, locked to `us-central1`]
- Pharmacy Integration Client -> External Pharmacy Systems: Sends e-prescriptions [HTTPS/REST]

## Technology Stack
- Node.js / TypeScript: Selected for the US FHIR Adapter to ensure rapid development, robust typing, and seamless integration with existing services.
- NestJS: Used for the FHIR Router/Controller to provide native dependency injection and strict DTO validation.
- GCP Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: Stores regional health data securely with strict geographic isolation (`us-central1` and `europe-west3`).

## Rationale
This component architecture enforces strict regional data residency and HIPAA compliance by isolating US operations within `us-central1`. The internal modularity of the US FHIR Adapter ensures reliable interoperability via HL7 FHIR standards while maintaining immutable audit trails.

EU E-Prescription Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It ensures strict regional data residency, compliance with GDPR and HIPAA, and local interoperability.

## Key Elements
* **Patients & Clinicians**: End-users accessing mobile and web clients.

* **EU E-Prescription Gateway**: Java / Spring Boot container for regional e-prescription integration.
* **Prescription Orchestrator**: Spring Batch/Core component managing workflow state.

* **External Pharmacy Systems**: National EU pharmacy systems using diverse standards.
* **Cloud SQL PostgreSQL & Cloud Storage**: GCP persistence layer restricted to `europe-west3`.

* **API Gateway -> Consent Enforcement Interceptor**: Routes EU-specific requests via gRPC over mTLS using signed JWTs.
* **Consent Enforcement Interceptor -> National Adapter Engine**: Internal dispatch after consent validation.
* **Prescription Orchestrator -> Cloud SQL PostgreSQL**: Persists region-specific data via JDBC (SQL/TCP, encrypted).
* **National Adapter Engine -> External Pharmacy Systems**: Integrates with national standards via mTLS, SOAP, and REST.

## Technology Stack
* **Java / Spring Boot**: Chosen for the EU E-Prescription Gateway due to robust enterprise integration modules (Spring Integration, Spring Batch).
* **GCP (europe-west3 & us-central1)**: Target cloud provider enforcing regional data residency.
* **gRPC / mTLS**: Used for secure inter-container communication.
* **PostgreSQL / Cloud Storage**: Persistent storage localized to regional GCP buckets and instances.

## Rationale
This architecture uses modular component decomposition within the EU E-Prescription Gateway to isolate regional data and satisfy GDPR residency constraints. Pluggable Spring Integration adapters handle heterogeneous EU pharmacy protocols while maintaining high accountability and consent enforcement.

Cloud SQL PostgreSQL & Cloud Storage.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, compliance, and interoperability across regional deployments.

## Key Elements
- Regional Database Instances: Cloud SQL PostgreSQL 15 deployed in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`.
- Encrypted Blob Storage: Google Cloud Storage regional buckets with CMEK via Cloud KMS.
- Audit & Compliance Ledger: PostgreSQL extensions, triggers, and Row-Level Security (RLS).
- Backup & Retention Manager: Cloud Storage Lifecycle Rules with object locks.
- Database Migration Manager: Flyway/Go schema migration component.

## Relationships
- Core Telehealth Service, US FHIR Adapter, and EU E-Prescription Gateway -> Regional Database Instances: Persist and retrieve regional data [PostgreSQL wire protocol / TLS 1.3].
- Core Telehealth Service -> Audit & Compliance Ledger: Write immutable symptom-checker logs and consent states [SQL / TLS 1.3].
- Cloud SQL -> Encrypted Blob Storage: Reference secure object URIs for media and prescriptions [Internal GCP API].

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Target cloud provider for regional isolation in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`.
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL 15: Primary relational database ensuring physical data residency.
- Google Cloud Storage & Cloud KMS: Secure object storage using Customer-Managed Encryption Keys.
- Flyway / Go: Database migration and schema management.

## Rationale
This architecture enforces GDPR and HIPAA compliance by physically separating regional data without default cross-region replication. It guarantees traceability for medical AI outputs and patient consent via immutable ledger patterns and regional CMEK encryption.
